quote: an exhaustible supply of mental energy
content: This is the "ego depletion" or strength model of self-control (Baumeister et al., 1998), and the depletable-fuel claim is now one of the more prominent casualties of the replication crisis. A preregistered, multi-laboratory Registered Replication Report found essentially no depletion effect (Hagger et al., 2016), and a meta-analysis correcting for publication bias put the true effect near zero (Carter & McCullough, 2014). Whatever limits self-control, the specific metaphor of a literal energy reserve that resisting temptation "uses up" is poorly supported.

quote: it contains more concentrated sugar, salt, and fat than anything that exists in the ancestral environment
content: The supernormal-stimulus concept itself is solid ethology: Tinbergen and colleagues showed that birds prefer exaggerated dummy eggs and that chicks peck hardest at exaggerated bill models (The Study of Instinct, 1951). Extending it to candy bars and video games is a reasonable analogy, but it is an analogy, not a measured result—"more than anything in the ancestral environment" is asserted rather than quantified, and the further leap to civilizational collapse is rhetorical. The ethological core is real; the sweeping cultural extrapolation outruns the evidence.

quote: have died playing online games for days without rest
content: These deaths are genuine but extraordinarily rare anecdotes, and a handful of cases cannot establish the population-level trend the essay extrapolates toward. The inference that market competition will ratchet games up to lethal addictiveness is a thought experiment, not a finding. "Gaming disorder" was added to the ICD-11 in 2019, but its status remains contested, prevalence estimates are low, and the diagnostic criteria are disputed—so the "marketed out of existence" thesis should be read as speculation rather than documented fact.
